bias.headline: Conditions are clearly bearish (led by Risk Appetite). This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBearish.label: Risk Appetite
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 1st percentile.
topBearish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 5.0% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 1% of them

topBearish.label: Market Breadth
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
topBearish.explanation: 46% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 27% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 58%.
topBearish.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 27% of them

topBearish.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing high rejected; no reclaim above 779.09
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 10 swing highs and 12 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 9% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
topBearish.explanation: SPY is printing lower highs and lower lows — an intact downtrend. Last swing high 773.09 vs prior 779.09; last swing low 759.97 vs prior 763.25.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
topBearish.nextTrigger: breaks up above the last swing high of 773.09

watchNext.label: Volatility
watchNext.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
watchNext.explanation: SPY typically moves 1.02% in a day right now — more volatile than 41% of its own past. That is unremarkable for this name.
watchNext.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only picks a side once it reaches the top or bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 41% of them, which is the middle

watchNext.label: Trend Strength
watchNext.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.05 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
watchNext.explanation: Over 60 sessions SPY moved -1.4%, and only 5% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
watchNext.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.05 now

metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this pair's own relative-strength history; current reading sits at the 17th percentile of it.
metrics.explanation: Over the last 60 trading days IWM is 4.7% behind the S&P 500. That is a wider gap than 17% of the readings in its own history against the index — so this is unusually weak for this name.
metrics.whyItMatters: An instrument that persistently lags its benchmark is not participating in the move, whatever its own chart says. Relative strength separates a rising tide from genuine demand.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 17% of them

metrics.label: Market Breadth
metrics.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
metrics.explanation: 46% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 27% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 58%.
metrics.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 27% of them

metrics.label: Trend Strength
metrics.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.15 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions IWM moved -6.1%, and only 15% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.15 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
metrics.confidenceBasis: 11 swing highs and 10 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 13% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: IWM is printing lower highs and higher lows — compressing into a coil. Last swing high 283.38 vs prior 287.21; last swing low 275.75 vs prior 270.44.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
conflicts: Range is narrowing; structure resolves on the break, and gives no direction until it does.
metrics.nextTrigger: resolves on a close outside 275.75–283.38

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.37% in a day right now — more volatile than 13% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
